##KM3NeT Digital Optical modules (DOMs)

##DOM definition
PMT shape is defined from the Hamamatsu R12199-02 scheme: Google Drive -> Detector Construction and operation (DET) -> Mechanics (MECH) -> All parts in a DU (drawings, pdfs, prices etc.)->common Arca+Orca -> DOM -> PMT (https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/0B-oDhZjfBP59V24wSGRsT1RBRWM).   -> R12199-02 Drawing 13.04.03.pdf

The reflector is defined according to file PMT+reflector position.pdf in the same folder.

PMT are placed and numbered according to the table 1 in Definition of DOM coordinate system and PMT map (File KM3NeT_DET_2014_002-PMT_map_v5.pdf in Google Drive -> Detector construction and operation (DET)  https://drive.google.com/drive/u/1/folders/0B6CcXapUNLNLc1hDek1VNTRXemM). PMT numbering is done accorging to the DAQ channel (column 2) and placement is done in spherical coordinates (theta, phi) - columns 4,5.

The DOM creation is described in GetDOM function of common/src/KM3OpticalModuleMgr.cc. Note that PMTs are placed in polar coordinates (theta, phi) directrly in this function according to PMTPositions entry in common/data/KM3OMkm3net.dat. Their type and sizes are also read from the same file. In future release this may be done in different way (using \"Place them\" method in common/src/KM3DetectorConstruction.cc.

The detector creation with one DOM is shown in common/data/KM3DetDOMAlone.dat. The DOM orientation is described with Euler angles (Phi, Theta, Psi) in the so-called "x-convention" (http://mathworld.wolfram.com/EulerAngles.html). The Psi entry is arbitrary (default is 0). For more details, please, read CLHEP User Guide (http://proj-clhep.web.cern.ch/proj-clhep/doc/CLHEP_1_7/UserGuide/index.html or http://proj-clhep.web.cern.ch/proj-clhep/doc/CLHEP_1_7/UserGuide/VectorDefs.ps) section CLHEP Vector -> HepRotation. The rotational convention are not obvious. After several tests the following strategy is suggested to obtain predictable results. If polar coordinats of an object main vertex are known and without rotation this vertex has (0,0,1) direction, then the polar coordinated of the final object placement can be obtained with following sequence (placed somewhere in the detector construction, for example):

    G4RotationMatrix* theRot = new G4RotationMatrix();  //create new rotation
    theRotPMT3->rotateZ(-phi);     //this is done first, counter clockwise rotation around Z for postive argument (so Y goes to X!), rotates axes too
    theRotPMT3->rotateY(-theta);   //this will be done second
    cout << "print rotation angles" << theRotPMT3->getPhi() << " " << theRotPMT3->getTheta() << " " << theRotPMT3->getPsi() << endl;

Note, that rotateX,Y,Z function rotate object and axes simultaneously counter clockwise. While Euler rotation rotate object and axes simultaneously counter clockwise.

##Angular Acceptance (AA) scans
AA scans are done with a parallel light beam covering all the DOM surface (Rbeam = 17''/2 inches). 
AA is calculated as number of photons detected per number of photons generated per generated beam circle area and expressed in cm^2 (so it is similar to the cross-section definition).
The simulation is performed in the water without scattering and absorption (ideal water).
It is used further in full detector simulation. The simulation is done at fixed wavelengths (energies from 2.035 to 4.135 eV with 21 steps of 0.1 eV) and fixed zenith angles theta (from 0 corresponding to light going antiparallel to the PMT direction to 180 hitting PMT from the back with steps of 1 degree).

###Scan of a DOM equpped with one bottom PMT
This is scan of a bottom PMT (DAQ ID 22). The DOM description is provided in common/data/KM3OMkm3netTest.dat where only one PMT is placed. The DOM itself is rotated upside-down in detector file (common/data/KM3DetDOMAloneTest.dat) and the light beam goes upside down for theta=0 as described in mac file (build/scripts/vis-AA2D.mac). The shell script (build/scripts/jobAA2D.sh) runs 21 executons of OMGsim for 21 energy steps and fixed theta angles. Shell script build/scripts/subAA2D.sh submits 180 jobs; one job for each angle.

To run the whole AA production do the following:

    cd build/scripts/
    source setenv.sh
    ./subAA2D.sh

Folder build/prod will be created and filled with output root files.
The AA table can be produced with makeAAtable.cc in PostAnalysis/scripts (not available in v2.0, but can be taken from trunk).

    cd PostAnalysis/scripts/
    root -l makeAAtable.cc

###Scans of a DOM with all PMTs installed

The scan with DOMs with all PMTs installed requires slightly different data analysis (which is in progress). For scans of PMTs different from the bottom one, the DOM should be placed in a way that this PMT looks up. This can be realized with three Euler angles. In general, Psi angle is also needed. The Psi angle is not implemented in v2.0 so, this scan can be performed only for the bottom PMT there.

To be continued...
